newsitem.title: USA: Arbitrage still pulling plug on US foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: Arbitrage still pulling plug on US foreign crudes.

text.p: The historically narrow arbitrage between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent was still pulling the plug on U.S. foreign crudes Wednesday, with refiners homing in on alternative domestic grades, traders said.
The Dec WTI/Brent spread is running around 33 cents a barrel, with import costs scarcely offset by the Dated Brent price.
The closed arb window has pumped up demand for Louisiana sweet grades in recent days, traders said.
Regional light sweet grades continued to turn heads. Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol was rumored to have sold a Cusiana cargo to Amoco at Jan WTI plus 29 cents fob.
Prompt Brent into the U.S. was notionally pegged at Dec WTI plus 15 cents on a delivered basis, traders said.
Brent for December arrival was assessed at Jan WTI plus 30 cif, with Cusiana heard offered at Jan WTI plus 45 cents fob.
Continued speculation is swirling around Statoil, which has five Brent cargoes without a clear destination as yet.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a Wall Street trader bought two partial cargoes of Jan Brent at $23.25 and $23.30 a barrel, down five to 10 cents from the IPE close.
Intermonth spreads were stronger, with one deal done at Brent Dec/Jan 35 cents, around parity with the late London session.
